articles.title: AJK govt announces phased restoration of internet services
articles.description: MUZAFFARABAD: The Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) government has announced a phased restoration of internet services across the region, with broadband and cellular data services to resume fully in some districts while access will remain restricted to educational institutions and banks in others. The Home Department, in a notification issued on Sunday, directed the secretary of the Ministry of Interior to initiate restoration of broadband and cellular data services from Monday (Aug 31) according to a district-wise schedule. Under the schedule, full broadband and cellular data services will be restored in Neelum district, including Upper and Lower Neelum, as well as Leepa Valley and Haveli district. Broadband services will also be restored throughout Bhimber and Mirpur districts. In Muzaffarabad district, broadband access will be confined to educational institutions — schools, colleges and universities — and banks. The same arrangement will apply in Jhelum Valley. In Bagh district, broadband services will be available only to educational institutions and banks within the municipal limits of Bagh and Dhirkot. Similarly, in Kotli district, broadband access will be restricted to educational institutions and banks, except in Sehnsa, Sarsawa and Tattapani where services will remain shut. No internet services will be restored in Rawalakot and Sudhnoti districts, where the suspension will continue. Bankers in the capital welcomed the restoration, saying it would ease pressure on branches that had been handling a heavy volume of customers in the absence of digital banking facilities. Ordinary citizens, however, expressed disappointment over the limited scope of the restoration, particularly those dependent on the internet for their livelihoods. Faisal Javed, president of the Association of Pharmacies and Medical Stores, said the suspension had severely disrupted electronic payments, leaving both traders and customers in difficulty. Internet services were suspended across AJK on June 5 amid a law and order situation following the government’s decision to proscribe the Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC). Published in Dawn, September 1st, 2026

articles.title: Windows 10 and 11 users are seeing a Defender warning that isn’t real
articles.description: Over the past few days, some Windows 11 users have been getting incorrect warning messages about Microsoft Defender—the operating system’s built-in security solution—being disabled. According to Microsoft in this Windows Health post , the warnings are caused by a bug that was introduced in the latest Defender updates: After installing the latest updates for Microsoft Defender Antivirus, notifications might appear stating that “Microsoft Defender Antivirus is turned off,” even though the antivirus is functioning correctly and all settings show it as active. These notifications can appear when Windows starts and intermittently afterward. They persist even if notification settings are turned off. Per Microsoft, this bug currently affects Windows 10 (versions 22H2, 21H2, Enterprise LTSC 2019, Enterprise LTSC 2016), Windows 11 (versions 26H1, 25H2, 24H2, and 23H2), and Windows Server (versions 2025, 2022, 2019, 2016, 2012 R2, and 2012). The bug is scheduled to be fixed in the next Defender update, which currently has no release date: Next steps: We are working to release a resolution in a future Microsoft Defender Antivirus update and will provide more information when it is available. Further reading: 5 Microsoft Defender settings I always change ASAP

articles.title: These 8 clever PC desk upgrades free up more space than you’d expect
articles.description: I write about cables, docks, peripherals, laptops, and all sorts of PC gadgets. Every day, random items wash up onto my desk, like a shipwreck after a storm. De-cluttering my desk is a priority...if only! Part of my problem is my setup. My father owned an antique rolltop desk, and I decided I wanted one too, full of nooks and crannies and drawers to store cables and pens and all sort of little geeky knickknacks. The problem is that those desks don’t really work with what I’d like to do: Organize my desk space using the accessories below. My plan right now is to possibly invest in a new workspace for my office, including the stylish, functional desk at the end of my list. But I’ll need to build it out with the necessary accessories to neaten, straighten, and de-clutter. This is my potential shopping list. Hopefully, it benefits you, too. (One theme you’ll see here: think vertical! Put stuff above or below your sightlines to reduce clutter.) Xpatee Under Desk Cable Management Tray: $15.99 Cable clutter comes in two forms: I/O cables like HDMI and Ethernet that can snake across your desk, and power cords to connect and power all of your gadgets. I’ve been considering a cable tray for a while now, and my colleague Alaina Yee owns and recommends this cable tr a y, by Xpatee . The point here is that it all lives underneath your desk, out of the way. Amazon This rather spacious (15.7 x 6.1 x 7.3 inches) wire mesh cable tray also includes four cable clips and six cable ties. It’s a clamping model which means that it might work for the lip that surrounds my rolltop, but it’s just the thing for a flat, traditional desk. Your desktop just has to be between 0.4 inches and 2.4 inches thick. It looks like it works best if your power cables can either go through a built-in cable port on your desk, or if your desk is pulled out slightly from the wall so that they can reach. View Deal CCCEI Mount Surge Protector: $35.99 A side- or under-mounted surge protector is another option; instead of placing a traditional surge protector in a bin like Xpatee does, this surge protector clamps onto your desk. This power strip has six outlets — not as many as some do, but arrayed on the top and side to allow for different types of plug arrangements. There’s always that odd plug (like a Google Home device, or a smartphone charger) that can throw the whole arrangement off. Also, there have been no complaints about the clamp strength, which can be an issue if you’re plugging or unplugging a cord or simply dealing with the weight of the assorted cables. There are USB-A ports and a USB-C port for charging, too. Amazon Note that I chose the version of this surge protector that pushes out 65W through the USB-C port, giving you an additional power option, as well as the 10-foot cord. Just be warned: The vast majority of clamping power strips do not carry UL certification, which means that they haven’t endured UL’s safety inspection. If that worries you, use a traditional UL-certified power strip with the cable-management tray, above, or Cable Matters’ 6-outlet desk-mounted power strip, for $41.99 . The only thing about the Cable Matters power strip, which I haven’t tried, is the mounting option. It’s a fixed shell of plastic with an adjustable flip-up latching mechanism? It’s definitely a little odd, and only supports up to 24W of USB charging. But it appears to be designed with safety in mind. View Deal MSI MAG MT201 Single-Monitor Desk Mount: $69.99 Clutter can include the monitor itself! A monitor mount allows you to raise and lower the display as you like, and move it around your desk to accommodate your position and ergonomics — or just get it out of the way. Our list of the best monitor arms highlights the MSI MAG MT201 for its combination of features and affordability. MSI This arm will need some assembly and setup, which differentiates it from the more expensive models. Still, it’ll support up to 44 pounds (way more than necessary), with an easy-release VESA screw to quickly add or replace and existing display. View Deal Ugreen Vertical Laptop Stand Holder: $19.98 If you own a laptop, you have a few options for how it sits on desk: on your desktop itself, up and out of the way on a laptop riser, or a third option: a vertical laptop stand. This Ugreen laptop stand holds the laptop vertically, and closed; the idea is that you’re using the laptop as a sort of a mini PC, with an external keyboard and display. Amazon Some of you might like to use that built-in display, especially if it’s an OLED or a high-refresh-rate display. But laid flat, any laptop takes up desk space. Placed on its edge, your desk space increases dramatically. This holder fits any laptop that’s between 0.47 and 1 inch think (from gaming to productivity devices), with a nice bit of cushy rubber to hold and protect your laptop. Ignore that Apple logo; it works with Windows laptops, too. View Deal SVNNELP Under Desk Drawer: $29.44 You’re always going to end up with little bits of stuff on your desk: staples, push pins, pens, cables, and more. How you deal with it is up to you, but one way is with an under-desk drawer. Amazon SVNNELP offers a trio of small, medium, and large desk drawers that you can pick and choose from. The kicker here is that they’re held on by strong adhesive, rather than screws. You can always opt for a more permanent screw-in model, but these sticky drawers work as long as you don’t store anything too heavy in them. View Deal OPNICE Desk Organizer: $21.99 One important point for desk organization that I mentioned earlier is to go vertical: A display that can be aligned vertical in portrait mode can improve a desk’s usable space. In this case, the OPNICE Desk Organizer is actually a monitor riser and a collection of bins to hold all of your extra stuff. Amazon If you’re like me, you raise your monitor up a bit via its stand or a riser. In this case, you’re using the extra space (20.5 x 9.5 x 6.3 inches) to good use. It’s all made of metal, and can support up to 44 pounds, which is way more than a traditional external display weighs. View Deal JAKO Headphone Stand: $6.95 I personally don’t have a need for a headphone stand or hook — but many people do, just to clear the last bit of gear off their desk. Amazon Jako’s headphone stand doesn’t do anything unique, but it clamps on to your desk and provides a home for your headphones. It’s available in three colors: black, white, and aluminum. View Deal Tribesigns 78.7-inch Computer Desk: $179.99 Now I do love my rolltop, but if I wanted to fully implement my de-cluttering plan, I’d need a new desk. I’m seriously considering this Tribesigns computer desk as an alternative for my home office, perhaps even two of them. Why two? I like being able to pivot between tasks, and an L-shaped desk is pretty ideal for my needs. My second choice, SEDETA’s $109 66-inch L-shaped desk , might even be too small. Sure, I’d lose a little space putting two Tribesigns in an L-shape, but the tradeoff is a generous amount of desktop, sufficient for an office setup as well as after-hours play space. Amazon The Tribesigns desk measures 78 inches wide, and 27 inches deep, and about 30 inches high. It’s made of 0.59 inch MDF wood, with metal legs. It’s sturdy and supports up to 200 pounds; the desk itself weighs about 60 pounds. Also, it ships in a variety of finishes, from a neutral walnut finish to coffee and an oak-like stain. Aside from a new desk, however, most of these improvements don’t cost all that much. With PC prices through the roof, maybe it’s time to save on the other stuff! View Deal
